newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed despite local funds support.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed despite local funds support.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed mixed on Monday, as foreign selling continued to dog blue-chips and local institutions partially supported the market with limited bargain-hunting activity.
At the close, the benchmark Composite Index of 100 leading issues slipped 0.98 of a point to 1,077.40, after having dipped as low as 1,067.20 in morning trading.
"It's the locals pushing up the index, because overall the market is negative. My order pad is full of sell orders," said a dealer at a large local brokerage house.
Among the most active issues was Telekom Malaysia.

Ekran Bhd jumped 55 cents to 5.55 ringgit after hitting a new low for the year earlier in the day. Analysts said they could see no fundamental reason for the stock's sudden rise, but said it may have been linked to the listing of the company's rights on Tuesday.

"There is a rumour that Ting (Pek Khiing, Ekran's chairman), may be looking to sell his stakes in PWE Industries Bhd and Granite to Ekran, and thereby increase his own stake in the company," said an Ekran analyst at a foreign brokerage house.
Market volume stood at 243 million shares, valued at 1,693 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 353 to 228.
A major local fund manager said it saw fundamental buying opportunities as the market was currently far below its levels at the start of the year.
"We are always in the market whenever there are bargains. We do look at those good fundamental buys," said a senior fund manager at the institution.

When asked about his opinions of Telekom and Malayan Banking, together contributing around 18 percent of the weighting of the Composite Index, he said: "If the price is right and if the fundamentals are good, then why not?".
"We still like Telekom inspite of the competition within the sector because the government still holds a significant share in the company.
The Malaysian government holds around 71 percent of Telekom.
Banking and finance group DCB Holdings gained 10 cents to 8.20 ringgit, with 4.7 million shares traded.
"Most fund managers look favourably at DCB after its restructuring with Rashid Hussain," said the fund manager.
On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot June contract shed one point to 1,074.9 with 699 lots changing hanbs. No other contracts were traded.
